analysis.investment_thesis: Malpani Pipes is a 2017-incorporated micro-cap (Rs 69 Cr) with a negligible 0.26% ROE — effectively no earning power despite a superficially low 7.84 P/E. Without a multi-year audited record of consistent profits, dividends, or balance-sheet strength disclosed, this fails my quantitative filters on every dimension that matters.
key_strengths: Low headline P/E of 7.84 suggests no speculative froth in the price
High promoter holding (73.78%) aligns insider interests
Small industrial manufacturer in a tangible, understandable business (plastic pipes)
key_risks: ROE of 0.26% indicates the business earns essentially nothing on equity — likely an accounting profit near zero
Recently listed micro-cap (incorporated 2017) lacks the 5-10 year earnings record I require
Negligible institutional ownership (FII 4.41%, DII 0.07%) — illiquidity and limited scrutiny
red_flags: ROE of 0.26% is a quantitative disqualifier — capital is not being productively deployed
P/E of 7.84 on near-zero earnings implies EPS is trivially small, making the ratio misleading
No disclosed book value, current ratio, debt/equity, or dividend history to verify margin of safety
analysis.detailed_analysis:
From a Graham perspective, the screening data here is disqualifying before any qualitative discussion. A 0.26% ROE means the company is essentially idle capital — on a Rs 69 Cr market cap that P/E of 7.84 implies roughly Rs 8.8 Cr in earnings, but the ROE math suggests either a tiny equity base or that profits are trivial. Either way, there is no "proven earning power" to anchor intrinsic value. I have no visibility into current ratio, debt-to-equity, interest coverage, or book value — and the absence of such data in an SME-scale listing is itself a red flag.

The company was incorporated only in 2017 and lacks the 5-10 consecutive years of positive earnings I demand. High promoter ownership at 73.78% is a neutral-to-mild positive but does not substitute for financial durability. Without evidence of a dividend record, a Graham Number calculation showing the stock below sqrt(22.5 × EPS × BVPS), or a current ratio above 2.0, there is no margin of safety here — only speculation on future capacity utilization. Mr. Market is not offering a bargain; he is offering an opaque micro-cap. Pass.
